SPCX.asOf: First post-IPO results, Aug 4, 2026 (from news coverage - Yahoo Finance/Reuters/CNBC summaries, not read from the filing itself)

guidance.label: Q2 net loss / EPS
guidance.value: $541M loss (improved by $467M); GAAP EPS -$0.09 vs -$0.23 expected

guidance.label: Connectivity segment (Starlink)
guidance.value: Revenue +66%, operating income +79%; subscriber base doubled

guidance.label: Capex
guidance.value: About $18.4B reported for the period; management warned spending would stay near that level (per a news report; verify in the filing)

guidance.label: Formal full-year guidance
guidance.value: Not confirmed in the coverage I read

deals.what: Multiple agreements for AI compute capacity; management credits them for the margin expansion in the quarter
Awarded multi-year US government contracts for Starshield satellite services
Enterprise and government demand continues to drive Connectivity growth
Merger with Elon Musk's AI lab added an AI reporting segment (X and xAI); the AI business is the main source of losses and capex
Two Starship V3 flight tests completed in the last 90 days, aimed at full and rapid reusability
Record IPO priced at $135 a share at a valuation above $1.7T
deals.size: Largest IPO on record per press reports

risks: Capex: roughly $18B in a period, driven by AI infrastructure, while the company still reports a net loss
Insider lock-up expirations ahead could add selling pressure (shares fell ~5% after the report on this and capex concerns)
The AI segment (X/xAI) lost far more than it earned in 2025 and is bundled with the profitable Starlink business
Valuation: priced for very high growth as a single instrument across launch, Starlink and AI
Key-person and governance concentration around Elon Musk

MRNA.asOf: Q2 2026 results release, Jul 31, 2026 (company press release; check later news for events after this date)

guidance.label: 2026 revenue
guidance.value: Up to 10% growth vs 2025; about 50% US / 50% international

guidance.label: H2 2026 revenue timing
guidance.value: About 55% of second-half revenue lands in Q3

deals.what: Unanimous advisory committee (VRBPAC) recommendation on June 18; would be Moderna's fifth approved product. Also under review in Europe, Canada and Australia
deals.timing: FDA decision date Aug 5, 2026 (outcome not verified here)

deals.what: Intismeran autogene (mRNA-4157) personalised cancer vaccine with Keytruda: 9 Phase 2/3 trials; 5-year Phase 2b melanoma data showed a 49% lower risk of recurrence or death vs Keytruda alone; Phase 3 melanoma data possible in 2026
Joint procurement contract for mRESVIA (RSV vaccine) on behalf of six countries
Collaboration supporting a COVID vaccine supply agreement
Long-term strategic partnership; COVID vaccine deliveries drove Q2 revenue
Expanded partnership

mCOMBRIAX (flu + COVID) approved in the EU and under review in Japan, Canada, Australia; awaiting FDA guidance on a US refiling. mNEXSPIKE approved in Japan and Taiwan; mRESVIA approved in Australia and Mexico
Propionic acidemia (mRNA-3927) registrational study fully enrolled; data possible in 2026. Decision on a methylmalonic acidemia pivotal trial deferred until then

risks: Still heavily loss-making: Q2 net loss $782M on $145M revenue; cash fell to $6.9B and a $950M settlement was paid in July
Revenue is small and lumpy: Q2 was $145M, up 2% year over year; guidance is only up to 10% growth
Norovirus vaccine (mRNA-1403) missed the Phase 3 interim criteria; the trial continues with an extra cohort
Heavy dependence on a few pipeline readouts (cancer vaccine, rare disease) and on regulatory decisions
Valuation allowance and no tax benefit; any further cash burn beyond $4.7-5.2B guidance would add pressure

guidance.label: Contracted power by year-end
guidance.value: 5 GW target (raised); >1 GW of new capacity per year from 2027

deals.partner: Reflection, Cohere, a US "neolab" and a US quant trading firm
deals.what: Four 1-3 year AI cloud contracts signed in Q2; upfront payments cover ~50-60% of the related capex
deals.size: Average >$1B each; $20-25M revenue per MW per year
deals.timing: Capacity comes online late 2026; revenue mostly 2027+

deals.what: Up-to-6-month capacity for time-bound needs (e.g. model releases), sold at a premium; one deal signed recently
Long-term contracts used to fund the build-out; management says all Microsoft capacity tranches due so far have been delivered, including at the Vineland site
$775M asset-backed facility secured in July against contracted cash flows, mid-single-digit rate; management calls the model repeatable
At-the-market share sales to fund growth
deals.size: $2.8B gross from 12.7M Class A shares at ~$224 average

deals.what: Eigen AI (inference and compression, ~$331M), Tavily (developer search for AI agents, ~$189M), ClarifAI (inference orchestration, ~$97M)
New model in which third parties finance, build and operate sites while Nebius supplies the platform and demand

risks: Capex of $20-25B against ~$3B of revenue: heavy dependence on prepayments, debt and share sales
Dilution: ATM sales of $2.8B so far
Lag between powered capacity and revenue (commissioning, cluster build, customer onboarding)
Local opposition and permitting risk for US data centers (e.g. a New Jersey hearing adjourned without a vote)
GAAP loss of $190M in Q2 even with positive adjusted EBITDA; customer and GPU-supply concentration

deals.what: Long-term agreement to develop and supply future TPU generations and AI networking; TPU v8i in production shipments
deals.size: "Multi-tens of billions" of dollars of TPUs per year
deals.timing: Next several years; demand grows into 2028-29

deals.what: Custom TPU capacity: Ironwood (v7) in 2026, TPU v8i in 2027, more in 2028. Expected to be Broadcom's largest XPU customer in 2027
"Jalapeno" custom accelerator shipping; next-gen XPU near tape-out; third-gen in development
Three generations of MTIA custom accelerators through 2027
AI XPV financing platform for OpenAI/Anthropic compute; third parties underwrite, Broadcom may give modest residual-value guarantees
deals.size: First $35B tranche closed June 2026 (Anthropic 1 GW); >20 GW targeted by end of 2028

deals.what: Singapore substrate fab starts FY27; laser capacity being roughly tripled; Tomahawk 7 (200 Tb/s) taped out

risks: Customer concentration: ~6 XPU customers drive most AI revenue
Data-center readiness: land, power, HBM, wafers and substrates can limit deployment pace
Gross margin dilution from memory-heavy XPUs (guided ~73% in Q4)
